content:
According to a recent report from The Guardian, Apple is participating in negotiations for the U.S. broadcasting rights to The Open Championship golf tournament. Netflix and Amazon are also expected to show interest in these broadcasting rights.

The Open Championship was first held in Scotland in 1860 and is the oldest of the four men's major golf tournaments, organised by The R&A. Americans occasionally refer to this tournament as the 'British Open' to distinguish it from the separately held U.S. Open.

In 2017, NBC outbid ESPN with a higher offer and signed a 12-year broadcasting rights deal with The Open. Versant also holds partial broadcasting rights and operates the Golf Channel. The R&A stated that they expect to hold discussions with NBC and Versant, as well as other parties interested in the broadcasting rights.

Today's report indicates that Apple has held 'preliminary discussions' with The R&A regarding bidding for The Open Championship broadcasting rights. The report cites a source 'familiar with Apple's plans' and notes that Apple 'remains committed to investing in sports broadcasting rights and will continue to identify suitable sports assets'.

A spokesperson for The R&A responded to The Guardian:

'Our partnerships with NBC and Versant have been excellent, bringing significant benefits to The Open, the AIG Women's Open, and our other tournaments and international events. Looking ahead to The R&A's next U.S. media rights cycle, we expect to engage with our existing partners NBC and Versant in due course. We will also continue to monitor the evolving broadcasting landscape and the broad interest in our rights from various parties.'

Last year, Apple announced a major partnership with F1, becoming the exclusive broadcasting partner for F1 in the United States. The company also streams Friday Night Baseball and Major League Soccer (MLS) matches.
